answer: Each identity must post a slashable bond from its own balance before earning. One wallet can mint a thousand aliases, but every alias pays the same bond again, so the attacker's capital at risk grows with the number of identities instead of staying flat. Rewards per identity are capped below the bond, so farming clones ties up more money than one honest node. Votes weigh stake, not head count, so a crowd adds no leverage and proven collusion burns the stake. The farm's atlas of names becomes a costly summit of locked value, not a cheap lotus opening.
